35.notes: This item carries an answer_challenge; I agree with it. As literally printed, the stem reads 4x − 5 = 3y/(4x − 5), which multiplies out to (4x − 5)² = 3y, giving x = (5 ± √(3y))/4 directly by square-rooting both sides. That expression matches none of the four printed options, so the stem as printed is unanswerable. The stem was almost certainly meant to read 4x + 5 = 3y/(4x − 5): multiplying by (4x − 5) then gives the difference of two squares (4x + 5)(4x − 5) = 3y, i.e. 16x² − 25 = 3y, which solves to x = ±√(3y + 25)/4. That matches option C once its garbled bracket placement (printed as ±(√(3y +) 25)/4) is read as ±√(3y + 25)/4. The hints and solution are written consistently for this corrected stem, disclose the misprint openly to the student, and keep the settled key C, which is the right way to teach an examiner error without arguing the student out of the key.
